method: Source inspection of the installed pinned host package (npm ci from integrations/openclaw/package-lock.json) plus the CI and VPS captures listed in attempted_routes. File digests were computed on the linux_host VPS and matched a second npm ci on the owner's MacBook byte for byte. Hook, middleware, provider and delegation behaviour below is read from the shipped code and documentation. The host calls and controls that the captures actually attempted are listed in attempted_routes; no stop point, middleware or retained borrow was exercised as a fence on a running host, and the routes named in attempted_routes.not_attempted were not called.

machine_runs.person_trial: setup_unavailable: private_network_unavailable (only a public IPv4 on eth0; no sudo; unprivileged user namespaces are restricted by AppArmor)
machine_runs.browser: Playwright 1.64.1 chromium-1248 and chromium_headless_shell-1248 lack libgbm.so.1 and libasound.so.2 (ldd: not found); no system packages installed

skill_loaded_use.question: A supported host point that can fence the next model request after skills_read as spec 7.6.1 requires: at that boundary it must re-verify fresh person authority, the session incarnation and the pinned bytes. A point that can stop delivery but cannot re-verify them does not count (spec 0.66 section 12.6.6).

surfaces.name: before_tool_call
surfaces.kind: gate (terminal block, fail closed on error/timeout)
surfaces.can_stop: the managed read (skills_read) before it runs
surfaces.context: agentId, sessionKey, sessionId, runId, toolCallId, abortSignal, requester{channel,accountId,senderId,senderIsOwner,roleIds}; the host keeps its executionIdentityToken/receiptAuthority receipt internal
surfaces.authority: none: no session access authority, no assertCurrent, no lifecycleRevision; hook contexts are excluded as authority by 7.6.2(2)

surfaces.name: api.registerAgentToolResultMiddleware
surfaces.kind: async tool-result transform before the harness feeds output back to the model; a throw replaces the result with a failure result
surfaces.can_stop: instruction bytes reaching the model (replaces the tool result); does not stop the model request itself
surfaces.authority: none (same as above); needs manifest contracts.agentToolResultMiddleware and explicit enablement

surfaces.name: provider wrapStreamFn / options.onPayload (RelayMind's own provider)
surfaces.kind: the provider transport for every model request of the composition; a throw in onPayload fails the request before it is sent
surfaces.can_stop: the next model request before HTTP dispatch
surfaces.context: ProviderWrapStreamFnContext: agentId, auth facts, model, extraParams, thinkingLevel, streamFn; per call: context.messages, options.sessionId
surfaces.authority: none by itself: no sessionKey, lifecycleRevision or person authority in its context; it sees the outgoing context.messages (so it can compare the delivered instruction bytes with the pinned contentHash) and options.sessionId. Combined with a retained session access borrow (GatewaySessionAccessAuthority.retain() below) it is the final boundary of a fence candidate
surfaces.verdict: stop without fence on its own; the stop of the retain() fence candidate

surfaces.name: before_agent_run
surfaces.can_stop: the run once, before its first model submission
surfaces.verdict: does not reach the post-read model request of the same run

surfaces.name: before_prompt_build (requiresToolAuthority, ctx.toolAuthority)
surfaces.kind: modify (prompt context, tool narrowing); with requiresToolAuthority a second, post-policy phase that receives ctx.toolAuthority {fingerprint, allows(toolName), assertActive()}
surfaces.can_stop: nothing: a thrown error or timeout is logged and skipped and other handlers' results are kept (hooks/reference.md, 'Log and skip the failed handler'); it adds prompt context or narrows the turn's tools only
surfaces.context: prompt, session messages snapshot, agentId, sessionKey, sessionId, runId, assertMemoryAudienceCurrent, hookInvocation.assertActive(); ctx.toolAuthority (PluginHookToolAuthority in config-contracts) only in the authorized phase
surfaces.authority: not person authority: ctx.toolAuthority checks the finalized tool surface of the active turn and rejects after the hook dispatch closes ('A retained toolAuthority object fails closed after dispatch'); its fingerprint 'is not a bearer token or authorization proof'. Spec 7.6.1 states the same: the tool fingerprint and hook lifetime are not person authority and alone do not establish that an exception aborts the host turn

surfaces.name: tool_result_persist, before_message_write
surfaces.can_stop: transcript persistence only; promises ignored, errors logged

surfaces.name: GatewaySessionAccessAuthority.retain()
surfaces.kind: original-person access borrow {signal, assertCurrent, release}, obtained with retain() inside a sessionAccess gateway method handler (RelayMind already registers relaymind.skill and relaymind.recommendations with sessionAccess {mode: write}); the documented use is a borrow that outlives the handler, 'for example for an interactive viewer'
surfaces.can_stop: nothing by itself; its assertCurrent() throws, and its signal aborts, when a check fails, so a provider onPayload that calls it before dispatch can stop the next model request
surfaces.authority: a supported native delegation (spec 7.6.1). In request-authorization (retain and assertActor) every assertCurrent() of the borrow re-runs, at call time: the captured operator run authority and the person's originalGrant assertCurrent(), the profile's isCurrent(), the current role's agent scope, the session check (same store path, store generation, sessionId and lifecycleRevision as the admitted target; reset, deletion or store replacement retire it) and the current tool policy and sharing. It subscribes to session changes, session identity mutation, profile and role policy changes and the source grant's signal, and on a failed check aborts its signal and releases. It does not check the invocation (invocationClosed is not part of the retained check), so it stays valid after the handler returns. It is not an earlier RPC's closed request scope or a JSON copy of its identity. Its scope, expiry and revocation have not been qualified
surfaces.verdict: fence candidate (with the provider onPayload stop and a pinned-byte comparison of the outgoing messages); not qualified and not excluded, so stop_point_absent is not established

surfaces.name: dispatchGatewayMethod (openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-method-runtime)
surfaces.kind: in-process dispatch inside an original authenticated plugin request
surfaces.authority: only within the original request scope; unavailable to hooks and the provider during a later agent run
surfaces.verdict: cannot re-run the fence's skills.library.read at use time

host_observations: CI run 41286397320: stale and deleted controls still delivered the pinned revision's bytes on the next turn (observed loaded_pinned_revision); the host keeps the session pin after a library head update or removal.

sessions.reset requires operator.admin (core-method-policy); the configured person policy lacks it. The native Control UI new-session control calls sessions.reset (declaring requiredScope operator.admin) only for a board session and otherwise sessions.create (control-ui-boot-chat).
skills_read takes only {name} (docs/tools/skills.md); the name resolves to the session pin on this host.
skill_loaded_use.conclusion: Points that can stop the read or the next request exist (before_tool_call, tool-result middleware, the provider's onPayload, before_agent_run). On their own none can re-verify fresh person authority, the session incarnation and the pinned bytes at that boundary, so on their own they do not count. But the host also offers a supported native delegation, the retained session access borrow of GatewaySessionAccessAuthority.retain(), whose assertCurrent() re-checks the original person's grant, profile, role, sharing and tool policy and the exact session incarnation at call time. RelayMind's provider could call it in onPayload before dispatch and compare the outgoing instruction bytes with the pinned revision. Spec 7.6.1 admits such a delegation once its scope, expiry and revocation are qualified. This search did not show that this composition fails, so stop_point_absent is not established and no negative skill_loaded_use record is made. skill_loaded_use stays disabled because it is unqualified, not as a host limitation; the open questions above decide it.
open_questions: Whether the provider's onPayload runs in the same process and realm as the gateway method handler, so that it can hold the retained borrow; not demonstrated on a running host.

Whether a borrow retained in a relaymind.skill or relaymind.recommendations RPC is the authority of the person whose turn reaches the provider (one borrow per session and person, matched by options.sessionId), and how long it lives (connection close, grant expiry, gateway restart).
Whether a throw in onPayload, or the borrow's aborted signal, prevents the HTTP dispatch on the pinned host; not exercised.

How the nonremoved library entry and the operator mapping that section 7.6.1 lists are re-checked at that boundary; the CI and VPS2 captures show the host keeps delivering the pinned revision after the entry is removed, so the fence itself would have to refuse it.
Revocation, reset and removal while a turn waits must be observed as a stop (section 7.6.1); none was tried.

mcp_use.question: A supported host route that invokes an independent, non-App MCP tool by its exact native identity (server/original/exposed name/schema/currentness tuple). MCP App view routes are App-scoped and do not count (spec 0.66 section 12.6.6; section 7.6.2 conditions 3 and 10).

routes.name: tools.invoke
routes.params: closed {name, args?, sessionKey?, agentId?, confirm?, idempotencyKey?, conversationReadOrigin?}

routes.name: mcp.app.callTool (and mcp.app.listTools)
routes.verdict: App-scoped: requires an active MCP App view bound to requester/session; independent tools have none, and no legitimate selected-asset-to-view binding exists in this composition. It does not count for exact_route_absent (spec 0.66 section 12.6.6; section 7.6.2 conditions 3 and 10); an App-specific trial would be a separate path, not tried here. Captures: mcp.app.listTools refused without a viewId.

routes.name: openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-tool-runtime (runAgentHarnessToolInvocation) and openclaw/plugin-sdk/codex-mcp-projection (materializeStaticMcpToolsForHarnessRun)
routes.verdict: documented private (harness-only, not for third-party plugins); calling a materialized tool's execute is excluded by 7.6.2(3)

routes.name: dispatchGatewayMethod -> tools.effective
routes.verdict: read-only discovery; invokes nothing. The pinned host returns {groups: [{tools: [entry]}], notices?}, with MCP entries carrying the host's server/original mapping. The VPS3 capture (checkout bba0cf1, after mcp.app.discover started the person session's MCP runtime) lists both colliding append tools under distinct exposed names (alpha-one__append for alpha.one, alpha-one-2__append for alpha?one); no server call was made. The earlier CI and VPS2 captures show an empty list only because their probe read payload.tools instead of payload.groups[].tools (fixed in be67556), and those runs did not start the session's MCP runtime first; the empty list was a harness projection, not a host result.

mcp_use.conclusion: No supported host route invokes an independent, non-App MCP tool by its exact native identity on 2026.10.7: tools.invoke is name-only, the harness tool runtimes are documented private, and mcp.app.callTool is App-scoped and does not count. Finding exact_route_absent (spec 0.66 section 12.6.6); mcp_use stays disabled and relaymind.mcp is not registered.

attempted_routes.note: Host calls and controls attempted on a running pinned host, as recorded in the committed captures. Each row names the capture and the recorded outcome.

mcp_use.outcome: started the person session's MCP runtime; no App view, no tool call
listed alpha-one__append (alpha.one/append) and alpha-one-2__append (alpha?one/append); read-only discovery

skill_loaded_use: GatewaySessionAccessAuthority.retain() borrow checked at the next model request
